chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah and Al-Himyari together, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to Sa'd ibn Abdullah
key_terms.السَّعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator and father of the author
key_terms.الْحَمِيرِيُّ: Al-Himyari, another narrator in the chain
key_terms.حَمَّادُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Hammad ibn Uthman, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith literature
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for the narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.يَعْقُوبُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ: Ya'qub ibn Yazid, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Hammad ibn Uthman's narrations verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a detailed verification of the isnad for narrations from Hammad ibn Uthman, a key figure in the Kufan scholarly circle, by tracing the chain through his father, Sa'd ibn Abdullah, and Al-Himyari. This cross-referencing underscores the reliability of the transmission via Ya'qub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, highlighting the meticulous attention to chain integrity characteristic of Shia hadith scholarship. Such clarification ensures the authenticity of the reports attributed to Hammad, reinforcing their standing in the jurisprudential corpus.
